raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Head-major GDP inputs already work, but backward returns update-major gradients that require copies to restore flattened projection channels. Return compact head-major dK/dV for these inputs so channel restoration is a view.

## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under LICENSE.txt.
- [x] I ran the changed-file repository pre-commit hooks and committed formatting.
- [x] I reviewed the applicable AGENTS.md Hard Rules.
- [ ] Maintainer assistance needed to apply labels (GitHub denied this account permission): `cat-feature`, `area:linear_attention`, `orig-external`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels / CuTeDSL and the GDP Torch wrapper.

## Summary

- Select K and V destination layouts independently; real/fake allocation and graph-cache identity agree.
- Extend the existing TMA descriptor-family machinery to dK/dV stores in the V64/V128, checkpoint/warmup and chain paths, preserving commit/wait ordering.
- Write grouped-head reductions directly into the selected destination.
- Add `test_gdp_head_major_grads` to the existing test module and document the policy.

Nine runtime files: +350/−89; one existing test file: +124; one existing documentation file: +16. [File responsibilities and validation evidence](https://github.com/bmac3/cudnn-frontend/blob/c6e0e8c25a63fc5353a7de69f9bf01d98b25a4c9/validation.md).

## Why

Logical `[L,U,H,D]` inputs with head-major inner strides `(D,U*D,1)` now receive compact gradient strides `(H*U*D,D,U*D,1)`. Then `grad.transpose(1,2).view(L,H*U*D)` shares storage. Regular token padding is compacted.

## Related issues

Closes #1747.

## API and compatibility impact

Automatic layout selection; no argument changes. Expanded-row and update-major gradient behavior is preserved, including U1 and mixed K/V inputs. Q/decay/output/sequence timelines and beta packing are unchanged. This does not widen the existing FROST hardware support; new execution evidence is GB300 SM10.3/BF16 only.

The direct-store tradeoff is measurable: 2.73% longer head-major backward alone and 28.37% less time for backward plus channel restoration (geometric means of paired case ratios). Existing update-major backward changed by +0.05% and head-major forward by +0.01% (geometric means). The largest head-major backward median was +4.06% for normalized H28, with paired rounds ranging from +2.94% to +6.51%. This does not establish end-to-end training speedup. [Per-case timings and paired-round ranges](https://github.com/bmac3/cudnn-frontend/blob/c6e0e8c25a63fc5353a7de69f9bf01d98b25a4c9/summary.md).

## Testing

Exact public base `d8b0a7ed56cd8e62bc1e05f367f339624f6dbb4e` versus head `fb753d71e874b4b1addb0515188372da7a279656`; each source package and native extension rebuilt together in separate environments, with module paths/hashes checked. A publication-time recheck found develop at `523f37d78fb90a8e82401b202dd90d281afd9cb7` (one later commit, no overlapping files); that newer revision was not measured.

- Public reproducer: base fails the requested stride contract; head passes compact/padded cases. Output, final state and all six gradients pass an independent FP64 oracle (maximum relative L2 error 0.355%).
- Focused pytest: 37 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (17 head-major and 20 existing token-major cases; 759.51 s). The suite checks bitwise values, exact strides, fake metadata, fresh cache entries, mixed layouts and autograd storage sharing.
- Regression control: the candidate test `frost-u3-v128-gva`, copied onto the exact unmodified base runtime, fails at the compact dK stride assertion after bitwise numerical checks pass (1 expected failure; pytest exit 1). The original base test file was restored afterward.
- Compute Sanitizer memcheck: V64/V128 equal-head direct-store cases passed (2 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; 91.64 s), and grouped-head reduction with normalization/coarse checkpointing passed separately (`frost-u3-v64-gqa-coarse-norm`: 1 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; 26.21 s). Both GDP runs reported **ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors** and exited 0. Valid/invalid detector canaries produced the expected exits 0/86.
- Pytest itself completed successfully; its original launcher then failed with a stale shared-file handle (job exit 2). The resumed sanitizer/benchmark job completed its workload with exit 0; details and logs are in the evidence.
- Black, Black-jupyter and SPDX hooks passed; clang-format had no applicable files.
- Benchmark: 10 cases completed; six sequential AB/BA rounds, 20 warmups and 100 samples per operation per round. Numerical/source-provenance and independent eager-versus-graph replay checks passed before timing; raw samples and allocation/storage evidence are published.

After [environment setup](https://github.com/bmac3/cudnn-frontend/blob/c6e0e8c25a63fc5353a7de69f9bf01d98b25a4c9/README.md), from `test/python`:

```bash
"$GDP_WORK_DIR/env-head/bin/python" -m pytest -p provenance -o addopts='' -n 0 -s -v --tb=short \
  linear_attention/test_la.py::test_gdp_head_major_grads \
  linear_attention/test_la.py::test_gdp_token_major_bitwise
compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --error-exitcode 86 \
  "$GDP_WORK_DIR/env-head/bin/python" -m pytest -p provenance -o addopts='' -n 0 -s -v --tb=short \
  'linear_attention/test_la.py::test_gdp_head_major_grads[frost-u3-v64-equal]' \
  'linear_attention/test_la.py::test_gdp_head_major_grads[frost-u3-v128-equal]'
```

[Portable reproducer, benchmark commands and raw logs](https://github.com/bmac3/cudnn-frontend/blob/c6e0e8c25a63fc5353a7de69f9bf01d98b25a4c9/README.md). No B200, FP16, full upstream suite, racecheck or training-throughput validation. Both standalone arms emitted existing nanobind reference-leak diagnostics at process exit. Kept draft for review of the layout policy and these validation limits.

 place; `dk`, `dv` and `dbeta` come back in the input's shape. `num_householder == 1` is exactly GDN.
 
+GDP selects compact head-major gradient storage independently for K and V when a rank-4 input has
+head-major inner strides: logical `[T, n, H, D]` with strides `(token_stride, D, n * D, 1)`.
+For these inputs, backward returns strides `(H * n * D, D, n * D, 1)`, including when the input's token
+stride has padding. This makes restoration to projection channels a view:
+
+```python
+kv = channels.view(T, H, n, D).transpose(1, 2)
+# After backward, dkv has the same logical shape and compact head-major storage.
+dchannels = dkv.transpose(1, 2).view(T, H * n * D)
+assert dchannels.data_ptr() == dkv.data_ptr()
+```
+
+Expanded-row and update-major inputs retain their existing gradient layout. Beta still requires unit head
+stride; packing head-major beta remains the caller's responsibility. Q, decay, output and sequence boundaries
+stay on the real-token timeline. This removes the separate K/V channel-restoration copies, not all backward temporaries.
+
 Mamba-2 uses the SSD vocabulary: `x` plays `v`, `B` plays `k`, `C` plays `q`, `dt` is the gate. The output is
 `y = C^T S + D x`, gated by `z sigmoid(z)` when `z` is given.
